name: 35 (2026-11-27 evening)
what: fresh verifier of B's G2; F continues its passage to 200 M and applies the corrections; C's corrections, conductivity reruns and G3 scope with the first bracket queued; D amends its G3 scope after the review and reads the guard test; core merges the source session and prepares release core-v0.9; the knowledge base reads the unread claims that tracks cite
note: Release core-v0.8 is on main (new runs use it). A candidate for core-v0.9 is published for scouting at scratch/core/exe/core_faces-finder/ (its card build is untested until core judges queue entry q0086): the horizon finder there has <fastflow> start_scan_<n> and trapped_tol_<n>; with release core-v0.8 already, <fastflow> flow = shear with mass_tol_<n> = 1e-5 and polish_iterations_<n> = 100 finds horizons of any mass from any start radius, and a continued run can switch on diagnostics with an input file. Rulings: coord/DECISIONS/0039 to 0048. KNOWN DEFECT of the shared queue, being corrected: a batch job that was preempted is listed as done; check with sacct that each job of a finished entry COMPLETED before you read its output, and add an entry again if it did not. After git merge main: nrpic-run finish closes runs continued in place; finish and verify keep a checksum cache. Close a finished run before you analyse it; every number with its run id; prediction before every new run or test; figures made by registered scripts and looked at; at most 6 cores.

items.title: fresh verifier for gate G2
items.task: Fresh verifier for gate G2 of this track (checklist item C18; decision 0016 item 4; coord/DECISIONS/0046 item 2 and 0048 item 3). About ninety minutes, processors only, no card run. If a full checksum pass of the stage check runs in the background (the lead says where its log is), leave it alone and report its result if it has ended. Trust nothing and do not read the lead's verdicts first (the outcome entries of the journals, stage/REVIEW-wave3.md, the verdict column of stage/G2/CHECKLIST.md): take what is claimed from the end of stage/G2/OPEN.md ('what to recompute first'), stage/G2/REPRODUCE.md and the ledger of note section VI, the criteria from the track's scope text, the predictions as they were written before the runs (git log shows when). With readers of your own, each tested on an analytic case first, recompute from the registered outputs: (1) the linear and expanding-box gravitational-wave tests the gate rests on (the exact solutions written by you); (2) the population box: the strain in the two gauges and on the two meshes with the Gamma-driver shift (the lead: 128 against 256 cells within 1.1 per cent to a = 64 and 2.8 per cent to a = 132), the high-k part with zero shift against the shifted gauge (the lead: 950 times smaller), halo counts and largest masses against the Newtonian mode with EQUAL particle masses (the particle files of relativistic runs carry the rest-mass weight), the stop of the zero-shift box at 256 cells; (3) the constraints: the mesh pair at eight particles per cell (the lead: the means fall 1.6 to 2.3 times when the spacing halves) beside one particle per cell (1.05 to 1.4), the particle leg; (4) the shearing-dust case: the run free of stream crossing (series 7: 0.053749, 0.053800, 0.053821; order 1.3) with your own check that no stream crosses before the rays arrive, and the case as run, which moved away from the reference code with each refinement and stays failed; (5) what G2 can claim and what it cannot (the halo catalogue is not mesh-converged at one particle per cell). A prediction before each recomputation, the outcome after it. Per claim: reproduced (to how many digits), not reproduced, or not checkable and why; predictions that failed as written are stated as failed. Figures you look at. Write stage/G2/VERIFIER.md; only after it is written, a last section that compares with the lead's verdicts.

items.extra: Extra for this session (about an hour). The independent review of gate G1 recommends a pass with reservations (stage/G1/GATE_REVIEW.md); decision 0048 item 2 says what comes before the tag. (1) FIRST: continue the passage from its last restart file to t = 200 M (the scope's criterion (iv) asks for the trackers to 200 M; the chain stopped at 186 M because Slurm refused one submission): one wrapper entry of the shared queue at priority 2, with the finder's diagnostics as before; prediction first (the lighter member's distance and speed at 200 M; the merged black hole's mass and spin). Check with sacct that its jobs COMPLETED. (2) The corrections of the verifier's second part (stage/G1/VERIFIER.md sections 16 and 17: 186 against 200 M; finding F1 decided for 86.6 to 131 M by the residual column, the upper branch being the converged surface; 'found' does not mean converged: horizon numbers quoted with the residual; the other items) and the gate review's list (note v3 with the passage, the schematics on the release, the figure title that still says partial). (3) When the continuation has ended: close it, read it with your registered readers, state the record to 200 M with the health checks in stage/G1/EVIDENCE.md and send the orchestrator one line (outbox) with the run ids: the gate is signed on that. If it has not ended by the end of the session, say where it stands. (4) Nothing of the passage's restart files is deleted (decision 0048 items 2 and 8); list their sizes per run in HANDOFF for a later decision.

Extra for this session (about seventy-five minutes). Gate G2 is signed, pass with reservations (coord/GATES.md; decision 0048 item 1): record it. (1) FIRST, so that they run while you write: the two conductivity runs whose intermediate snapshots were deleted (heat_C1, heat_C2) again on the release build with a reduction that writes into its own run directory (0.4 card-hours, priority 2), prediction first (the value 1.020 +- 0.004 is reproduced within what?). (2) The corrections the gate review lists: stage/G2/VERIFIER.md where the stage tool finds it; C18 judged; the full-pass VERIFY_RESULTS committed and the two heat runs named in OPEN.md; EVIDENCE and STAGE_REPORT regenerated; the verifier's requests (a) to (e); in the note: the compared value is the maximum of the binding energy (the source rejects the turning-point principle), no 'converged location', 'a finite-N effect' for the controls. Bring scope/SCOPE.md in line with decision 0048 item 1 with the date (the criterion of decision 0013; the two families as the first step of G3). (3) The scope of G3, written BEFORE any production run and reviewed independently before production: first step, the brackets of the King family with b = 0.1 and of the monoenergetic family at a million particles on two meshes, with the horizon finder of core-v0.8 (<fastflow> flow = shear, mass_tol 1e-5, polishing, diagnostics = true: a collapse is a found horizon from now on), at least three seeds for the members next to the threshold; then the collapsed mass fraction against the Knudsen number: the statistic and estimator, the reference, criteria with numbers fixed in advance and what would refute each, convergence legs that can fail (a slicing or domain-size leg, not only the shift damping), the whole-system budget with the collisionless drift, the card budget within 80 card-hours and the order of runs. Commit and push it; queue only the first step's bracket members for b = 0.1 (four entries at most, predictions first).

Extra for this session (about seventy-five minutes). The independent review of your G3 scope (g3/scope_review/SCOPE_REVIEW.md; decision 0048 item 4) says: do not queue the production set as written. (1) Check its three blocking findings from its artefacts with numbers of your own (the block count and cost of the finer mesh member and the smoke-test rule that rejects any such deck; the claim that fails by construction through a clock borrowed from the nearest tracer label, when each particle's own proper time is in the snapshots; the power of the convergence criterion as written), then amend scope/SCOPE_G3.md, each amendment dated and the earlier wording kept, with the should-change items too; predictions for the amended criteria in the journal; commit and push before any production entry. (2) The excision-guard test EG8 (queue entry q0085): if its job has COMPLETED (check sacct), close it and judge E1 to E8 with a registered analysis and a figure; if not, say where it stands. (3) Then queue what the amended scope allows as its first step (the review names what can proceed), four entries at most, priority 2 for what the gate waits for.

items.task: Round for core without writing new source (about seventy-five minutes). (1) Merge origin/core/faces-finder (the source session of 2026-11-27: journal tracks/core/JOURNAL-faces-finder.md, its entry 6 lists the shared lines; changelog section 'Candidate for core-v0.9') into core/nrpic on processors: build, the byte regression against .work/build_cpu_v08 (75 items: all identical is the prediction, since no item uses compensation or deposit_fine_shape on a refined mesh), the tests of the branch (dep_levels.py, diag_restart.py with case a now expected to start, the finder tests on Track A's restart files), the quick tests. (2) The card check q0086 (core-ff-card): if its job has COMPLETED (check sacct: the queue lists preempted batch jobs as done), close it and judge it with tracks/core/analysis/faces_finder/card_check.py (journal entry 6 has the commands), figure looked at; if it was preempted, add it again at priority 2. (3) Write tracks/core/RELEASE-v0.9.md (NOT RELEASED until the card check has passed; then final, in the form of RELEASE-v0.8.md), the changelog section core-v0.9 (four options or changes, three changes without an option and which runs they change, what is not done: level faces between ranks, the cost of the compensated deposit), executables under scratch/core/exe/core_nrpic_v09/ only when final. (4) The byte comparison of the release builds .work/build_cpu_v08 and .work/build_gpu_v08 against core_nrpic_v08 that the clerk asked for; record it in RELEASE-v0.8.md. (5) Inbox: Track A's requests on the finder (answered by the source session: say so), Track F's on diagnostics at restart; Track A now names the outer outflow faces as the place where its constraint ratio fails to converge (decision 0048 item 5): say which options of core-v0.6 for the outer faces (<z4c> ghost_falloff, sbc_variant = nonwave) apply to its expanding ball and what test would show their effect. Records, commit, push core/nrpic.

items.title: the unread machine-located claims that a track cites
items.task: Claims package of the knowledge base, fifth, continuing claims4 (tracks/kb/claims4/README.md, LEDGER.tsv, scripts; decision 0048 item 7). About ninety minutes, processors only. Class T of claims4 (144 claims located by machine, never read by a person, and cited by a track's note or checklist) has 131 unread members: read them at every stored locator in the raw sources, in the seeded order of claims4, as many as the time allows; a prediction first of how many are not right as worded (claims4 measured 10 of 13 right in this class). For each: right as worded; superseded by a whole-sentence claim with the correct label (a track's own judgement or reading stored as 'fulltext' gets the label judgement or is withdrawn); or withdrawn. Apply by a plan file with the package's apply script, dry run first. Tell each owner (one information note per owner) which of the claims it cites changed and how, with the place in its files where the claim is cited. The rate with its interval beside the earlier samples; a figure; a new snapshot and the QA run. LEDGER, README, JOURNAL with outcomes.
